library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

```{r model-meta}
mod <- readModelDb("RamosMartin_2017_teicoplanin")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.00707-17> (open access in PubMed Central,
  PMC5610524)

Ramos-Martin and colleagues pooled the teicoplanin concentrations of two Liverpool
studies -- one in neonates, one in children older than 1 month -- into a single
population model that could serve as the Bayesian prior of a BestDose
multiple-model dose controller. The model was fitted non-parametrically with the
NPAG algorithm in Pmetrics. No supplementary material accompanies the article,
and no erratum was found (Europe PMC search, 2026-11-25).

# Population

Fifty-seven patients contributed 394 concentrations (Table 1): 18 neonates
(postmenstrual age 26-44 weeks, median weight 2.04 kg), 16 infants and toddlers
aged 1-23 months, 20 children aged 2-11 years and 3 children aged 11-16 years.
Overall median age was 0.88 years (0.01-15.82), median weight 7.5 kg
(0.69-62.2), 24 of 57 were female, median Haycock-Schwartz eGFR was 62.06
mL/min/1.73 m^2 (5.4-160.3) and median serum creatinine 41 umol/L (21-308).
Patients were treated for proven or suspected methicillin-resistant
staphylococcal sepsis or central-line infection; 40% were in intensive care,
mostly after cardiac surgery, and 30% were oncology patients with febrile
neutropenia. Neonates received a 16 mg/kg loading dose then 8 mg/kg daily as a
30-min infusion; older children received 10 mg/kg every 12 h for three doses
and then 10 mg/kg daily as a 2-5 min bolus.

```{r population}
str(ui$population[c("n_subjects", "n_observations", "age_range", "weight_range", "sex_female_pct")])
```

# Model structure

Two-compartment model with zero-order intravenous input (Eqs. 2a and 2b):

* `kel = Ke0 * (WT/70)^-0.25 * Renal`, `V = V0 * (WT/70)`;
* `Renal = PNA (days) / SCr (umol/L)` when postnatal age is below 3 months
  (age < 0.25 year), otherwise `Renal = eGFR^pw` (eGFR uncentred, in
  mL/min/1.73 m^2);
* `Ke0` and `V0` take one value for samples drawn < 96 h after the first dose
  (the paper's occasion 1) and another from 96 h onward (occasion 2). The
  packaged model switches them as a step at 96 h after the first dose
  (`tafd()`), so the concentration is discontinuous there by the ratio of the
  two volumes. `Kcp`, `Kpc` and `pw` are shared.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment ODEs with `kel` as above | -- | Methods, Eqs. 2a and 2b |
| Output `Y = X(1)/V` | -- | Methods, text after Eq. 2b |
| `Renal` switch at age 0.25 year | -- | Methods, text after Eq. 2b; Table 3 footnote |
| Occasion split at 96 h | -- | Methods, 'There were two sampling periods'; Table 3 footnote |
| `lkel_lt96h` (Ke01) | log(0.03) 1/h | Table 3, median |
| `lkel_ge96h` (Ke02) | log(0.025) 1/h | Table 3, median |
| `lvc_lt96h` (V01) | log(19.52) L | Table 3, median |
| `lvc_ge96h` (V02) | log(22.7) L | Table 3, median |
| `lk12` (Kcp) | log(0.23) 1/h | Table 3, median |
| `lk21` (Kpc) | log(0.12) 1/h | Table 3, median |
| `e_crcl_kel` (pw) | 0.07 | Table 3, median |
| `e_wt_kel` | -0.25, fixed | Eq. 2a; Methods 'we chose to fix these values' |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1, fixed | Table 3 footnote, 'Volume = V0 * (wt/70)' |
| `etalkel_lt96h` | 0.745755 | Table 3, CV = 0.04/0.038 |
| `etalkel_ge96h` | 0.527355 | Table 3, CV = 0.03/0.036 |
| `etalvc_lt96h` | 0.333034 | Table 3, CV = 14.23/22.636 |
| `etalvc_ge96h` | 0.117921 | Table 3, CV = 7.95/22.472 |
| `etalk12` | 0.672740 | Table 3, CV = 0.48/0.490 |
| `etalk21` | 0.952369 | Table 3, CV = 0.27/0.214 |
| `etae_crcl_kel` | 0.891998 | Table 3, CV = 0.15/0.125 |
| `addSd`, `propSd` | 0, fixed | not reported (assay-error polynomial unpublished) |

Every omega is `log(CV^2 + 1)` with `CV = SD / mean` of the NPAG marginal.

# Typical values against the Abstract

The Abstract summarises the model as `Ke = 0.03 * (wt/70)^-0.25 * Renal` and
`V = 19.5 * (wt/70)` with `Renal = eGFR^0.07` or `PNA/SCr`. The packaged model
must return exactly these on its first occasion. The two reference patients of
the dose-controller simulations (Methods) are used, plus a median neonate from
Table 1.

```{r typical-values}
pts <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3,
  who = c("Infant (Fig. 5)", "Child (Fig. 6)", "Median neonate (Table 1)"),
  WT = c(6.3, 16.3, 2.04),
  PNA = c(0.46 * 12, 5.78 * 12, 17 / 30.4375),
  CREAT = c(40, 40, 44.5),
  CRCL = c(63.84, 108.41, 42.8)
)
ev_tv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pts$id, function(i) {
  data.frame(id = i, time = c(0, 1, 100), amt = c(10, NA, NA), evid = c(1, 0, 0), cmt = "central")
})) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pts[, c("id", "WT", "PNA", "CREAT", "CRCL")], by = "id")
tv <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev_tv, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 1) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pts[, c("id", "who")], by = "id")
renal_expected <- ifelse(
  pts$PNA < 3,
  pts$PNA * 30.4375 / pts$CREAT,
  pts$CRCL^0.07
)
kel_expected <- 0.03 * (pts$WT / 70)^-0.25 * renal_expected
vc_expected <- 19.52 * pts$WT / 70
tv_tab <- data.frame(
  Patient = tv$who,
  kel = signif(tv$kel, 4),
  `kel (Abstract)` = signif(kel_expected, 4),
  `vc (L)` = signif(tv$vc, 4),
  `vc (Abstract)` = signif(vc_expected, 4),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(tv_tab, caption = "Typical kel (1/h) and central volume on occasion 1.")
stopifnot(
  max(abs(tv$kel / kel_expected - 1)) < 1e-10,
  max(abs(tv$vc / vc_expected - 1)) < 1e-10
)
```

## Unit of postnatal age in the young-infant renal descriptor

The Methods text defines the young-infant descriptor as "the PNA (in years)
divided by the serum creatinine concentration (in micromoles per liter)", while
Table 1 reports PNA in days and the Abstract does not say. The two readings
differ 365.25-fold, and Table 3 decides between them. `Ke0` is one parameter
estimated across all 57 patients, so if PNA were in years, the neonates'
`Ke0` support points would have to sit about 365 times above those of the older
children to give comparable elimination. The reported `Ke0` distribution (mean
0.038, SD 0.04 1/h) leaves no room for that.

```{r pna-units}
med_neo <- c(WT = 2.04, PNA_d = 17, SCR = 44.5) # Table 1, neonates
size <- (med_neo[["WT"]] / 70)^-0.25
kel_days <- 0.03 * size * med_neo[["PNA_d"]] / med_neo[["SCR"]]
kel_years <- 0.03 * size * (med_neo[["PNA_d"]] / 365.25) / med_neo[["SCR"]]
# Ke0 a median neonate would need under the years reading to keep the same kel
ke0_needed_years <- kel_days / (size * (med_neo[["PNA_d"]] / 365.25) / med_neo[["SCR"]])
data.frame(
  reading = c("PNA in days", "PNA in years"),
  `kel at Ke0 = 0.03 (1/h)` = signif(c(kel_days, kel_years), 3),
  `half-life of kel (h)` = signif(log(2) / c(kel_days, kel_years), 3),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median Table 1 neonate (2.04 kg, PNA 17 days, SCr 44.5 umol/L).")
# Under the years reading, 18 of 57 patients would need Ke0 near ke0_needed_years.
# Their contribution alone to the mean of the Ke0 marginal would exceed 3 1/h, far
# above the reported mean of 0.038 1/h (about 90-fold).
stopifnot(18 / 57 * ke0_needed_years > 50 * 0.038)
```

The days reading gives an elimination half-life (of `kel`, before
distribution) of about a day; the years reading gives one of about a year. The packaged model therefore uses
days, converting the canonical `PNA` column (months) with `PNA * 30.4375`.

# Structural check: ODE against the closed-form two-compartment solution

Within the first occasion all parameters are constant, so a bolus must follow
the two-compartment biexponential exactly. This checks the micro-constant
wiring of Eqs. 2a/2b.

```{r closed-form}
cf_pts <- pts[1:3, ]
ev_cf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cf_pts$id, function(i) {
  rbind(
    data.frame(id = i, time = 0, amt = 100, evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
    data.frame(id = i, time = seq(0.25, 95, by = 0.25), amt = NA, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  )
})) |>
  dplyr::left_join(cf_pts[, c("id", "WT", "PNA", "CREAT", "CRCL")], by = "id")
sim_cf <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev_cf,
  returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
)
cf <- sim_cf |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    a = kel + k12 + k21,
    alpha = (a + sqrt(a^2 - 4 * kel * k21)) / 2,
    beta = (a - sqrt(a^2 - 4 * kel * k21)) / 2,
    closed = 100 / vc * ((alpha - k21) / (alpha - beta) * exp(-alpha * time) +
      (k21 - beta) / (alpha - beta) * exp(-beta * time))
  )
max_rel_err <- max(abs(cf$Cc / cf$closed - 1))
max_rel_err
stopifnot(max_rel_err < 1e-6)
```

# Occasion 2: steady-state exposure via PKNCA

From 96 h onward the second-occasion `Ke0` and `V0` apply, so at steady state the
dosing-interval AUC must equal `dose / (kel * vc)` evaluated on occasion 2. The
three reference patients receive the label regimen used in the study (neonate:
16 mg/kg then 8 mg/kg daily as a 30-min infusion; infant and child: 10 mg/kg
every 12 h for three doses then 10 mg/kg daily) for 40 days, and PKNCA computes
the last interval.

```{r ss-pknca}
mk_regimen <- function(id, wt, neonate) {
  if (neonate) {
    times <- seq(0, 39 * 24, by = 24)
    amts <- wt * c(16, rep(8, length(times) - 1))
  } else {
    times <- c(0, 12, seq(24, 39 * 24, by = 24))
    amts <- rep(10 * wt, length(times))
  }
  data.frame(id = id, time = times, amt = amts, evid = 1, cmt = "central", rate = amts / 0.5)
}
ev_ss <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pts$id, function(i) {
  rbind(
    mk_regimen(i, pts$WT[i], pts$PNA[i] < 3),
    data.frame(
      id = i, time = c(seq(0, 48, by = 1), seq(39 * 24, 40 * 24, by = 0.25)),
      amt = NA, evid = 0, cmt = "central", rate = NA
    )
  )
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pts[, c("id", "WT", "PNA", "CREAT", "CRCL")], by = "id")
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ev_ss,
  returnType = "data.frame",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pts[, c("id", "who")], by = "id")

conc_ss <- sim_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, who, time, Cc)
dose_ss <- ev_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pts[, c("id", "who")], by = "id") |>
  dplyr::select(id, who, time, amt)
nca_ss <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ss, Cc ~ time | who + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | who + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 39 * 24, end = 40 * 24,
    auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
  )
))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_ss$result) |>
  dplyr::select(who, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
last_dose <- dose_ss |>
  dplyr::group_by(who) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(time, n = 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(who, last_amt = amt)
expected_auc <- sim_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 40 * 24) |>
  dplyr::select(who, kel, vc) |>
  dplyr::left_join(last_dose, by = "who") |>
  dplyr::transmute(who, auc_expected = last_amt / (kel * vc))
nca_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(nca_tab, expected_auc, by = "who") |>
  dplyr::mutate(rel_diff = auclast / auc_expected - 1)
nca_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(auclast, cmax, cmin, auc_expected), ~ signif(.x, 4)),
    rel_diff = signif(rel_diff, 3)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Patient = who,
    "AUC0-24 day 40 (PKNCA, mg*h/L)" = auclast,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin,
    "Dose / CL, occasion 2 (mg*h/L)" = auc_expected,
    "Relative difference" = rel_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value steady state on occasion 2.")
# Linear trapezoid on a 0.25 h grid: measured error up to 6e-4 (the neonate), so the
# bound has about 8-fold headroom.
stopifnot(max(abs(nca_cmp$rel_diff)) < 0.005)
```

```{r ss-plot, fig.cap = "Typical-value profiles over the first 48 h under the study's label regimens."}
sim_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 48) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = who)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(15, 60), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Teicoplanin (mg/L)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Monte Carlo regimen comparison (Results, last paragraph)

The paper simulated 100 profiles per regimen for four loading/maintenance
regimens and reported, for the best one -- three loading doses of 25 mg/kg every
12 h then 10 mg/kg daily -- that 30% of patients reached a day-3 trough of 15-60
mg/L and 13% exceeded 60 mg/L. The simulation used the Pmetrics non-parametric
prior with covariates "in the same range as the original population"; neither
the covariate sampler nor the support points are published.

The cohort below is built to match Table 1: 18/57 neonates and 39/57 older
children, with log-normal draws around the Table 1 medians and redrawn
(not clipped) outside the Table 1 ranges. Children's weights follow a median
weight-for-age curve with 15% scatter. Doses are given as 30-min infusions;
maintenance starts 24 h after the last loading dose, and the day-3 Cmin is the
minimum concentration between 48 and 72 h.

```{r mc-cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2017)
draw_ln <- function(n, med, sdlog, lo, hi) {
  x <- numeric(0)
  while (length(x) < n) {
    y <- exp(rnorm(n, log(med), sdlog))
    x <- c(x, y[y >= lo & y <= hi])
  }
  x[seq_len(n)]
}
# Approximate median weight-for-age (kg), both sexes averaged.
wt_for_age <- stats::approxfun(
  c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16),
  c(3.3, 6, 7.8, 9.6, 12.2, 14.3, 16.3, 18.3, 20.5, 25.6, 31.9, 40.5, 50.8, 58.6)
)
n_per_arm <- 200
n_neo <- round(n_per_arm * 18 / 57)
n_child <- n_per_arm - n_neo
age_child <- draw_ln(n_child, 3.3, 1.1, 0.12, 15.8)
wt_child <- wt_for_age(age_child) * exp(rnorm(n_child, 0, 0.15))
cohort <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    PNA = draw_ln(n_neo, 17, 0.8, 4, 69) / 30.4375,
    WT = draw_ln(n_neo, 2.04, 0.45, 0.69, 5.08),
    CREAT = draw_ln(n_neo, 44.5, 0.5, 21, 265),
    CRCL = draw_ln(n_neo, 42.8, 0.5, 5.4, 95.2)
  ),
  data.frame(
    PNA = age_child * 12,
    WT = wt_child,
    CREAT = draw_ln(n_child, 41, 0.4, 27, 308),
    CRCL = draw_ln(n_child, 78.94, 0.45, 6.43, 160.3)
  )
)
cohort$id <- seq_len(nrow(cohort))
summary(cohort[, c("PNA", "WT", "CREAT", "CRCL")])
```

```{r mc-sim}
regimens <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("(i) 3 x 30 then 20", "(ii) 3 x 20 then 15", "(iii) 3 x 25 then 10", "(iv) 2 x 30 then 10"),
  load = c(30, 20, 25, 30),
  n_load = c(3, 3, 3, 2),
  maint = c(20, 15, 10, 10)
)
mc_one <- function(r) {
  ld_t <- (seq_len(regimens$n_load[r]) - 1) * 12
  md_t <- max(ld_t) + 24 * (0:3)
  doses <- data.frame(
    time = c(ld_t, md_t),
    mgkg = c(rep(regimens$load[r], length(ld_t)), rep(regimens$maint[r], length(md_t)))
  )
  ev <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cohort$id, function(i) {
    rbind(
      data.frame(
        id = i, time = doses$time, amt = doses$mgkg * cohort$WT[i], evid = 1,
        cmt = "central", rate = doses$mgkg * cohort$WT[i] / 0.5
      ),
      data.frame(id = i, time = seq(48, 72, by = 0.5), amt = NA, evid = 0, cmt = "central", rate = NA)
    )
  })) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cohort, by = "id")
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::summarise(cmin = min(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = regimens$regimen[r])
}
mc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), mc_one))
mc_tab <- mc |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    in_window = mean(cmin >= 15 & cmin <= 60),
    above_60 = mean(cmin > 60),
    median_cmin = median(cmin),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    published_in_window = c(NA, NA, 0.30, NA),
    published_above_60 = c(NA, NA, 0.13, NA)
  )
mc_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-regimen, ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Regimen = regimen,
    "Cmin 15-60 (simulated)" = in_window,
    "Cmin > 60 (simulated)" = above_60,
    "Median day-3 Cmin (mg/L)" = median_cmin,
    "Cmin 15-60 (published)" = published_in_window,
    "Cmin > 60 (published)" = published_above_60
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fraction of subjects by day-3 Cmin window (mg/kg doses).")
```

```{r mc-plot, fig.cap = "Day-3 Cmin by regimen; dashed lines mark the 15-60 mg/L window."}
ggplot(mc, aes(regimen, cmin)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(15, 60), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Day-3 Cmin (mg/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The simulated fraction in the window for regimen (iii) is higher than the
published 30%, and more subjects exceed 60 mg/L. The comparison is shown but
not asserted. The window fractions depend on the covariate sampler, which the
paper does not describe, and on the shape of the parameter distribution, which
here is a log-normal approximation to an unpublished non-parametric prior. They
also count threshold crossings, which are sensitive to both. What does carry
over is the paper's qualitative conclusion: no fixed weight-based regimen
places most of the cohort in the 15-60 mg/L window by day 3.

```{r mc-assert}
# Qualitative claim above. With 200 subjects the binomial SE of a fraction near
# 0.45 is about 0.035, so the 0.75 bound sits about 8 SE above the rendered values.
stopifnot(all(mc_tab$in_window < 0.75))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PNA unit.** The young-infant descriptor uses PNA in days, not the years
  printed in the Methods; see "Unit of postnatal age" above.
* **Age switch.** "Age < 0.25 year" is implemented as canonical `PNA < 3`
  months (0.25 x 365.25 = 91.3 days = 3 months at 30.4375 days per month).
* **Typical values are NPAG medians**, as quoted in the Abstract. Every
  marginal has its mean above its median, so the right skew is at least
  qualitatively consistent with a log-normal.
* **Inter-individual variability** is a log-normal approximation with
  `CV = SD / mean` from Table 3. The non-parametric joint distribution, and so
  any correlation between parameters or between the two occasions, is not
  published; all etas are independent. In particular, a simulated subject's
  `Ke0` and `V0` are redrawn independently at 96 h.
* **Occasions as a step at 96 h after the first dose.** The paper assigns
  occasion 1 to samples drawn < 96 h and occasion 2 to samples drawn >= 96 h
  after treatment initiation. The packaged model applies the second-occasion
  values from `tafd() >= 96` without resetting the compartment amounts, so the
  concentration jumps by `V0_lt96h / V0_ge96h` at that time.
* **Residual error** is `fixed(0)`. Observations were weighted by the inverse of
  the estimated assay variance, but the Pmetrics assay-error polynomial and any
  gamma/lambda term are not reported. The assay's own precision (< 6%,
  Methods) is not a model residual and is not used.
* **eGFR** is used uncentred (`eGFR^pw`) exactly as printed. It is the
  Haycock-Schwartz estimate with k = 0.33 / 0.45 / 0.41 for preterm neonates,
  term neonates and older children; users should compute it the same way.
* **Not reproduced:** the BestDose individual dose optimisation (Figs. 5-6,
  Table 4) uses each patient's Bayesian posterior over the unpublished support
  points, so it cannot be replicated from the population model.
